newsitem.title: GREECE: NATIONAL SECURITIES SAYS 96 PRETAX PROFIT ROSE 65PCT.
newsitem.headline: NATIONAL SECURITIES SAYS 96 PRETAX PROFIT ROSE 65PCT.

text.p: Athens stock exchange member and National Bank subsidiary National Securities said its 1996 pretax profit rose 65 percent to 1.1 billion drachmas from 673 million a year earlier.
"The rise in profitability was helped by the firm's involvement in the trading of bonds, new relationships with foreign institutional investors and successful cost containment," the company said.

The brokerage is about to complete its administrative and organisational overhaul. The changes will include the installation of tape recording facilities at the trading floor terminals that will provide a record of telephone conversations, it said.
Pending its board's approval, National Securities staff will be able to trade for their own account as long as a set of company regulations are met.
These specify that orders must be placed through National Securities only with staff required to submit a detailed statement of their trading account to the board monthly.
Incentives for better staff performance will include bonuses linked to productivity.
And NIBID, another National Bank subsidiary, will acquire a significant stake in National Securities this year.

The brokerage arm of National Bank eyes growth capitalising on its parent's extensive branch network and will try to attract a good chunk of the foreign institutional investor business, it said. Up until 1995 it did very little in this domain.
It plans to get more active in the secondary bond market and further develop relationships with domestic institutional investors.
National also plans to strengthen its presence in the market for derivative products. Along with Merrill Lynch and Sigma Securities last year it launched a warrant on OTE telecom.

Its research department which recently recruited analyst George Karousos, formerly with Smith Newcourt and Sigma Securities, will be issuing company reports with buy, sell, hold recommendations, it said.
